ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: The sex-determination mode of goats is XY type. The pedigree chart in the figure shows the inheritance of a certain trait in goats; the dark color in the figure indicates individuals expressing this trait. It is known that this trait is controlled by a pair of allelic genes. Under the condition of not considering chromosomal variation and gene mutation, answer the question: Suppose the gene controlling this trait is located only on the Y chromosome. According to the inheritance law of genes on the Y chromosome, in generation Ⅲ, which individuals have phenotypes that do not conform to the inheritance law of this gene? (Fill in individual numbers)

The pedigree chart in the figure shows the inheritance of a certain trait in goats; the dark color in the figure indicates individuals expressing this trait. Under the condition of not considering chromosomal variation and gene mutation, answer the question: Suppose the gene controlling this trait is located only on the Y chromosome. ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the pedigree chart, squares represent males, circles represent females, and dark color represents individuals expressing this trait. There are 4 individuals in generation Ⅲ: Ⅲ-1 is a dark square male, and his father is Ⅱ-1, a light-colored square male; Ⅲ-2 is a light-colored circle female; Ⅲ-3 is a dark circle female, and her father is Ⅱ-3, a dark square male; Ⅲ-4 is a light-colored square male, and his father is also Ⅱ-3, a dark square male. Then reason: If the gene controlling this trait is located only on the Y chromosome, then this trait can only be carried and expressed by males, and the father's Y chromosome is passed only to sons, not to daughters. Therefore, all sons of an expressing father should express it, and sons of a non-expressing father should not express it; females should not express it. Checking generation Ⅲ one by one: the father of Ⅲ-1, Ⅱ-1, does not express it, but Ⅲ-1 expresses it, so this does not conform; Ⅲ-2 is female and does not express it, so this conforms; Ⅲ-3 is female but expresses it, so this does not conform; Ⅲ-4 is the son of Ⅱ-3, and Ⅱ-3 expresses it, so according to Y-linked inheritance he should express it, but Ⅲ-4 does not express it, so this does not conform. Therefore, in generation Ⅲ, those that do not conform to the inheritance law of the Y chromosome are Ⅲ-1, Ⅲ-3 and Ⅲ-4.
